newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU examining Dutch swine fever vaccine request.
newsitem.headline: EU examining Dutch swine fever vaccine request.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Wednesday the EU executive was looking into the possibility of using vaccines to help control the outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands.

Maintaining the Commission's general opposition to animal vaccination, Fischler said EU scientists would look into the use of so-called "marker vaccines", which the Dutch hope will help them identify and segregate infected animals more easily.
"This needs to be discussed, I have put the matter to our scientists," Fischler told journalists after EU farm ministers had agreed a farm price package for the coming year.

He said the Commission was generally opposed to using vaccines on animals because of the implications for the single market -- some shops have said they would not stock meat from vaccinated animals, and for the potential impact on trade.
Dutch Farm Minister Jozias van Aartsen has said the Netherlands wanted a "marker" vaccine in use by the end of the year.

The outbreak of swine fever, mainly in the south of the country, has led to the destruction of some three million pigs and cost more than a billion guilders, with most of the bill footed by the European Union. --David Evans, Luxembourg Newsroom +352 57262
